title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 is misfiring — incomplete combustion detected by the PCM.
fullDescription: DTC P0301: Cylinder 1 misfire detected. The PCM monitors crankshaft acceleration on each power stroke; if cylinder 1 fails to contribute, a misfire is logged. Persistent misfires can dump raw fuel into the catalytic converter and cause expensive damage.
safetyImpact: Continued driving with an active misfire can overheat and destroy the catalytic converter. Reduce load and have it diagnosed promptly.

causes.cause: Damaged wiring or connector at coil/injector

symptoms: Check engine light on (flashing during active misfire)
Rough idle or shaking at stoplights

fixSteps.title: Scan and Confirm
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze frame and live misfire counters. Confirm cylinder 1 is the highest counter; note RPM, load, and temperature when the fault sets.

fixSteps.title: Swap Coil and Plug
fixSteps.instruction: Move the cylinder 1 ignition coil and spark plug to a known-good cylinder. If the misfire follows the part, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Test Injector and Compression
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector resistance and listen with a noid light or stethoscope. Run a compression and leak-down test to rule out mechanical issues.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring and Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Check wiring and connector at cylinder 1 coil and injector. Repair shorts, opens, or corrosion; replace failed components.

faq.q: Can I drive with a single-cylinder misfire?
faq.a: Briefly and gently — a flashing CEL means severe misfire and you should not continue. Steady CEL is less urgent but still damages the cat over time.

faq.q: Will premium fuel fix it?
faq.a: Only if the root cause is carbon or low-grade fuel knock. Most misfires are mechanical/electrical and need parts.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fix?
faq.a: A coil and plug DIY is under $100. A failed injector or compression issue can run several hundred to over a thousand at a shop.

title: Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
shortDescription: Misfire detected during the first 1000 revolutions after a cold start.
fullDescription: DTC P0316: Misfire detected during the first 1000 revolutions after a cold start. The PCM uses crankshaft position data to track each power stroke; multiple cylinders missing or sensor faults log this code. Diagnose global causes (fuel, timing, sensor) before single-cylinder repairs.
safetyImpact: Random misfires can starve power on demand and damage the catalyst. A flashing MIL means stop driving and tow.

causes.cause: Worn spark plugs across the engine

fixSteps.title: Scan and Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Pull all codes including pending. Check for vacuum leaks with smoke or carb cleaner; verify fuel trims and crank sensor signal.

fixSteps.title: Verify Fuel Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Measure fuel pressure at idle and snap-throttle. Compare to spec; replace filter or pump if low.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect CKP/CMP sensors for damage and correct air gap. Scope the signal during cranking to verify pulses.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed component, clear codes, and confirm fix with a road test and follow-up scan.

faq.q: Why does my engine misfire only when cold?
faq.a: Cold misfires usually point to fuel injector, ignition coil, or compression issues that worsen with thicker oil and tighter clearances.

faq.q: Should I replace all coils at once?
faq.a: If they're original and high-mileage, yes — it saves diagnostic time and prevents the next failure.

faq.q: Will a tune-up fix this?
faq.a: Spark plugs, air filter, and PCV are a good first pass for random misfires — they often resolve the issue.
